title: Why You Can Smell Rain Before It Hits
hook: Every time you smell rain, you are actually smelling bacteria.
script: Every time you smell rain, you are actually smelling bacteria. Could your own nose really out-smell a hunting shark? Falling raindrops trap air against the ground, launching microscopic aerosols into the wind. This mist carries geosmin, the bacterial compound behind the fresh scent of petrichor. A shark tracks blood in seawater, but you detect geosmin at parts per trillion. A single speck in an Olympic pool is enough to trigger your nose. Did our ancestors evolve this superpower to find water, or to avoid poisoned springs?
